finding: Cardboard Trade (Solana) — oracle price path / exchange settle auth
attack_path: None found. The exchange's price-settle instruction (tag 0x1f) takes the settlement price DIRECTLY in its instruction data, so the whole system reduces to: (a) can an unprivileged caller invoke exchange tag 0x1f, and (b) can an unprivileged caller make the oracle compute a chosen price. (a) NO: exchange 0x1f is caller-gated to the oracle program — a top-level call carrying the exact same 35-byte payload and the exact same account list the oracle's CPI uses returns err=None but logs 'ORCLSKIP' and consumes only ~1361 CU (no-op); prepending an oracle push, appending/prepending the oracle program account, the oracle PDAs, or the Instructions sysvar account does not change that. (b) NO: the oracle push (top-level data 0x071f) is permissionless, but it validates every price-source account against a HARDCODED allowlist of program ids (BiSoNHVp.., TessVdML.., goonuddt.., ojh19oja.., AQU1FRd7.., ALPHAQmeA.., dijkbkCA.., fastC7gqs..) plus specific account keys (DmocjvFXp75.. owned by ojh, 8mZVRgrr.. owned by fast); any non-matching source is rejected and skipped (ORCLSKIP) — verified by a swap matrix in which every source-account substitution (same-owner or wrong-owner) produced ORCLSKIP. The source programs' price accounts are written by authorised updater signers (dijk<-FTp1BybZ51NiZKbnZH6MsrV3tUZNauhpQMbBcqYUEr5f, fast<-AK9U2FvVU12TjCoaGAnuvzNfZkuny4NiQZEkUBVK1Swz, BiSo<-7RrqWam5ri2Yu6fUtiCp2dwqaydjJYMXz6HtCnQPGbDY), not permissionlessly, so a fake price cannot be injected into a source. Net: no unprivileged path to an attacker-chosen settlement price; the ~$1.04M USDC vault is not reachable this way.

evidence.detail: exchange.asm:18108 is the exchange entrypoint; oracle entrypoint is at 0xa2c8. Oracle top-level push tag is 0x07 (data bytes 0x07 0x1f = base58 'YS'), 60 occurrences in 20 recent oracle txs.

fn_8480 loop: for each enabled source group, call fn_8480; if its return low-byte != 0x1a the group is SKIPPED and ORCLSKIP (0x50494b534c43524f) is logged via sol_log_64_. Loop index mask 'jge r3,0x6' => up to 6 source groups.

Source-group validation: for group index r8, compares 4 words of the candidate account's owner against a HARDCODED program-id allowlist taken from data_03c8|data_0488|data_04b8 / data_03f8 / data_0428 / data_0458 (6 entries, base58-decoded = BiSoNHVpsVZW2F7rx2eQ59yQwKxzU5NvBcmKshCSUypi, TessVdML9pBGgG9yGks7o4HewRaXVAMuoVj4x83GLQH, goonuddtQRrWqqn5nFyczVKaie28f3kDkHWkHtURSLE, ojh19ojaKduoJZuaJADhcVGp4xt1TcdAvZmpVsCorch, AQU1FRd7papthgdrwPTTq5JacJh8YtwEXaBfKU3bTz45, ALPHAQmeA7bjrVuccPsYPiCvsi428SNwte66Srvs4pHA). data tables at oracle.asm:13424-13429.

dijkbkCAKfFTCxQg3u1pg82gVU1jJGHBBRcteD11mBu (lines 4952-4955), ojh19oja.. (5000-5003) and fastC7gqs2WUXgcyNna2BZAe9mte4zcTGprv3mv18N3 (5007-5010) are compared as OWNER program ids of specific source groups (branch on r8==2/3/else).

Specific source ACCOUNT keys are hardcoded: account 37 must equal DmocjvFXp75asezCDKVNH2qaXbjrV7VeQk4aLZaPF88E (owner ojh) [lines 4840-4866], account 31 must equal 8mZVRgrrDjbhGdb6TSfHbhwoB4FoGDfo6D231PM7GDfW (owner fast) [lines 5032-5055].

Swap matrix (simulateTransaction, sigVerify=false): BASELINE=0 ORCLSKIP; EVERY source-account substitution (same-owner e.g. Tess32->35, dijk15->18; wrong-owner e.g. ->exchange-owned) produced >=1 ORCLSKIP. => source accounts are validated by exact key+owner, not merely by owner.

With ALL 10 source accounts replaced by non-source accounts: 5 ORCLSKIP logged, yet err=None and the oracle still writes the CTFEED01 feed (1338B) and CTWGHT02 weights (191B) and still CPIs the exchange successfully (cu ~7036 vs 16915 baseline). => a push with no valid sources falls back to the registry's last-known prices (stale refresh), it does not produce an attacker-chosen value.

Exchange instruction dispatch: first 8 bytes == 0x544e56455443 ('CTEVNT') => event instruction; else 1-byte tag dispatch over 0x00..0x2d. Tag 0x1f -> jmp_208d8 -> jmp_21290 (requires data_len==0x23=35) -> jmp_21f90 with handler-id r6=0x4.

Handler-id r6=0x4 (tag 0x1f) selects r3=0 -> jmp_22dc8, the caller/authority gate; other handler ids take a different branch. jmp_22dc8 calls fn_05d0 with r4=[r10-0xca8] (program id) and requires return 0x1a.

fn_05d0 compares the passed 32-byte program id against the HARDCODED oracle id (lines 236-243) and exchange id (lines 273-280), derives the PDA for the seed and compares to the passed account key; returns 0x1a on match. Gate fails => ORCLSKIP at exchange.asm:20020.

DIRECT exchange 0x1f with the exact oracle-CPI account list [20,41,3,8,42] and exact 35-byte payload: err=None, log 'ORCLSKIP, 0x1, 0x1f, 0x0, 0x3', 1361 CU (no settle). The oracle's own CPI of the SAME instruction succeeds (oracle push cu ~17000, exchange inner consumes ~4200 CU).

Bypass probes all bail: (1) +oracle program account appended, (2) +oracle PDA appended, (3) +weights appended, (4) oracle program prepended to account list, (5) a real oracle 0x071f push as instruction 0 followed by the direct exchange 0x1f, (7) Instructions sysvar first in account list => all ORCLSKIP, ~470-1361 CU. Only the oracle's own CPI settles.

Decoded CPI payloads: exchange tag 0x1f = [0x1f][u16 market_idx][u64 price][u64 price][u64 timestamp][u64 seq]; e.g. ix0 '1f00007bc6860a130000007bc6860a130000003e50701b00000000a14e160000000000' (market 0, price 0x130ac6867b). The self-CPI is the CTEVNT event, 140 bytes, discriminator 0x435445564e540000 ('CTEVNT'), NOT tag 0x0e.

On-chain identity: DmocjvFX.. (624B) and 8mZVRgrr.. (128B) are data accounts owned by the ojh / fast programs respectively; ojh, fast, dijk are executable (BPFLoaderUpgradeable). 5AVyF6qJ.. (8552B) owned by AQU1FRd7...

blockers: Exchange tag 0x1f settle is gated on the immediate caller being the oracle program; no unprivileged caller can satisfy it (verified by direct-call + bypass probes).
Oracle price sources are validated against a hardcoded program-id allowlist AND specific account keys; invalid sources are skipped (ORCLSKIP), so a fake source cannot be injected.
Source-program price accounts are updated by authorised signer accounts, not permissionlessly, so source data cannot be forged.
Oracle instruction data is only 2 bytes (0x071f) — no price can be supplied by the caller.

Residual (not fully quantified): a permissionless push with ALL sources invalid still writes a feed and settles using the registry's last-known prices (stale refresh). Impact is bounded by the last valid price and the keeper's constant pushes; not an arbitrary-price primitive.

Not reversed/verified: the exact caller-check instruction in the exchange (empirically only the oracle's CPI passes; the exchange imports sol_get_sysvar and contains the Instructions-sysvar id, so a sysvar-based caller read is the likely mechanism), the oracle_learning.rs deviation/TWAP logic, and the exact aggregation across the 5 source groups.

Not observed/tested: no top-level (user) exchange instructions appeared in 200 recent exchange signatures (all 571 invocations were inner 0x1f/CTEVNT from the oracle), so deposit (0x05)/withdraw/margin auth was not exercised.

oracle_top_level.0x07: push/update prices (data 0x07 0x1f = base58 'YS'); permissionless; 3x per keeper tx

exchange_inner_cpi_from_oracle.0x1f: settle/apply oracle price — data [0x1f][u16 market_idx][u64 price][u64 price][u64 ts][u64 seq]; caller-gated to oracle program

exchange_dispatch_table.note: 1-byte tag dispatch over 0x00..0x2d (exchange.asm:20572-20605) plus the 6-byte 'CTEVNT' event instruction; no top-level exchange tags observed live

method: sbpf disassemble on both ELFs; lddw->pubkey decoding; simulateTransaction (solders, sigVerify=false, replaceRecentBlockhash=true) against live mainnet state; getSignaturesForAddress/getTransaction tag census. Read-only; no transaction signed or sent. Public RPC api.mainnet-beta.solana.com.
